story: S002: Hook Validation and Quality Assurance
story_description: Provide comprehensive validation capabilities for hook configurations before export, ensuring configurations are syntactically correct, semantically valid, and follow best practices to prevent runtime failures in Claude Code and other CLI providers.
task_description: Create HookValidator actor that validates HookConfiguration objects, checking for structural errors, missing required fields, invalid patterns, and potential issues that could cause runtime failures or unexpected behavior.
atom_description: Implement HookValidator actor with ValidationResult, ValidationError, and ValidationWarning structs. Provides validate() method for HookConfiguration validation including matcher checks, hook entry validation, and hook definition validation. Includes validateJSON() method for raw JSON syntax checking. Actor isolation ensures thread-safe validation operations.
problem_statement: Hook configurations created in the visual builder or edited manually can contain errors that would cause runtime failures in Claude Code. These include missing required fields, empty hook arrays, invalid matchers, malformed command strings, and incorrect event types. Without pre-export validation, users may deploy broken configurations that fail silently or produce unexpected behavior. We need a comprehensive validator that catches these issues before export and provides actionable error messages.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Create new file HookValidator.swift in Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/ directory
Step 2: Import Foundation for JSONSerialization support
Step 3: Declare public actor HookValidator with no stored properties (stateless)
Step 4: Define ValidationResult struct as public and Sendable with isValid, errors, and warnings properties
Step 5: Define ValidationError struct as public Sendable with Identifiable conformance computing id from path plus message
Step 6: Add path (String) and message (String) stored properties to ValidationError
Step 7: Define ValidationWarning struct as public Sendable with Identifiable conformance computing id from path plus message
Step 8: Add path (String) and message (String) stored properties to ValidationWarning
Step 9: Implement public func validate(_ config: HookConfiguration) -> ValidationResult method
Step 10: Initialize empty errors and warnings arrays at method start
Step 11: Iterate over config.hooks dictionary using for (event, entries) in config.hooks pattern
Step 12: For each entry, construct base path as hooks.{event}[{index}]
Step 13: Check if entry.matcher.isEmpty and append warning about matching all if true
Step 14: Check if entry.hooks.isEmpty and append error about no hooks defined if true
Step 15: Iterate over entry.hooks with enumerated() to get hook index
Step 16: Construct hook path as {basePath}.hooks[{hookIndex}]
Step 17: Call hook.validate() to get array of HookDefinitionError results
Step 18: For each error in results, check isWarning property and append to appropriate array
Step 19: Use error.localizedDescription for the message field, defaulting to empty string if nil
Step 20: After all validation, construct ValidationResult with isValid = errors.isEmpty
Step 21: Implement public func validateJSON(_ json: String) -> Result<Void, Error> method
Step 22: Wrap JSONSerialization.jsonObject call in do-catch block
Step 23: Return .success(()) if parsing succeeds, .failure(error) if it throws
Step 24: Add documentation comments for all public types and methods

HookValidator.validateJSON(_ json: String) -> Result<Void, Error> - validates raw JSON syntax without semantic checks
ValidationResult.isValid: Bool - true if no errors found (warnings allowed)
ValidationResult.errors: [ValidationError] - array of blocking validation errors
ValidationResult.warnings: [ValidationWarning] - array of non-blocking validation warnings
ValidationError.id: String - unique identifier for SwiftUI List keying
ValidationError.path: String - dot-notation path to error location
ValidationWarning.id: String - unique identifier for SwiftUI List keying
ValidationWarning.path: String - dot-notation path to warning location

edge_cases: Edge case 1: Empty config.hooks dictionary - returns valid result with no errors or warnings
Edge case 2: Event with empty entries array - loop body does not execute, no errors produced
Edge case 3: Entry with nil matcher (if optional) - treat as empty, produce warning
Edge case 4: HookDefinition.validate() returns empty array - no errors or warnings added for that hook
Edge case 5: HookDefinitionError with nil localizedDescription - use empty string for message
Edge case 6: Very long path strings (deeply nested) - no truncation, full path preserved
Edge case 7: Duplicate errors (same path and message) - both included, id collision handled by SwiftUI
Edge case 8: Unicode characters in event names or matchers - handled correctly by String interpolation
Edge case 9: validateJSON with empty string - returns failure with JSON parsing error
Edge case 10: validateJSON with whitespace-only string - returns failure with JSON parsing error
Edge case 11: validateJSON with valid but non-object JSON (array, string) - returns success (valid JSON)
Edge case 12: Config with 1000+ hooks - completes within timeout, no stack overflow
failure_modes: FM1: HookConfiguration has unexpected structure - guard clauses return empty ValidationResult
FM2: HookDefinition.validate() throws exception - catch and convert to ValidationError
FM3: Memory exhaustion with huge error list - rely on system memory limits, no explicit handling
FM4: JSONSerialization throws non-standard error - wrap in generic parse failure message
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Core/Hooks/HookValidator.swift file. Remove any imports of HookValidator from HookExportService or other files that use it. Export functionality will proceed without pre-validation (user responsibility to ensure valid config). No persistent state or data affected.

notes: HookValidator is a critical component for preventing runtime failures. By validating configurations before export, users get immediate feedback on issues rather than discovering them when Claude Code fails to execute hooks. The actor design ensures thread safety when validation is triggered from UI updates. Consider extending with more semantic checks in future iterations.

risks: Risk 1: HookDefinition.validate() method may not exist yet, requiring stub implementation
Risk 2: HookDefinitionError protocol may need definition if not present
Risk 3: Validation may miss edge cases that cause runtime failures in Claude Code
Risk 4: Path notation may not match user expectations from JSON editors
Risk 5: Performance may degrade with very large configurations
mitigations: Mitigation 1: Define minimal HookDefinition.validate() returning empty array as stub
Mitigation 2: Define HookDefinitionError protocol with isWarning and localizedDescription
Mitigation 3: Add integration tests with real Claude Code to verify validation catches real issues
Mitigation 4: Use standard JSON path notation matching popular tools like jq
Mitigation 5: Add performance tests and optimize hot paths if needed
risk_register.blast_radius: Limited to hook export flow. If validator has bugs, worst case is false positives blocking valid exports or false negatives allowing invalid exports. No data loss risk. Users can bypass by editing settings.json directly.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If HookValidator proves problematic, export can proceed without validation with user acknowledgment. Add warning banner indicating unvalidated export. No persistent state affected.
